title: Suffering and God's Purpose
definition: Suffering and God's purpose is the truth that God remains sovereign, wise, good, and near even when His people suffer.
summary: Suffering is painful, but God can work through it with wisdom, mercy, and purpose.
christFocus: Jesus entered suffering, bore sin, and brings hope to sufferers through His cross and resurrection.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Suffering is one of the deepest realities of life in a fallen world. Scripture does not offer shallow answers or pretend pain is small. It shows that God hears, sees, comforts, disciplines, refines, sustains, and redeems.

God's purpose in suffering is not always immediately visible. Some suffering remains mysterious. Yet the cross proves that God can work through the darkest evil to accomplish redemption.

Believers can bring sorrow, questions, and weakness to God. They do not have to understand everything in order to trust the character of the One who gave His Son.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People in suffering often feel forgotten, punished, or useless. This doctrine matters because it anchors them in God's presence and purpose without minimizing their pain.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring suffering honestly to the Lord. Receive comfort, seek wise support, and keep obeying one step at a time. Let the cross remind you that God is present even when His purposes are hidden.
